extracted.intended_audience: state environmental agencies, regulated entities (industry), EPA staff, and public stakeholders commenting on or implementing EPA rulemakings
extracted.subtask_description: Summaries of EPA final rule actions and approvals (e.g., SIP approvals, delegation of authority, pesticide tolerances, NSPS/EG amendments) that state the legal/regulatory standards and conditions the Agency used to evaluate submissions or to apply regulatory requirements. Useful for preparing comments, compliance plans, or state submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: SIP interstate transport requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Clean Air Act (CAA) requires each state implementation plan (SIP) to contain adequate provisions prohibiting emissions that will significantly contribute to nonattainment or interfere with maintenance of air quality in other states.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to evaluate SIP revisions addressing interstate transport for specific NAAQS (example given: 2012 PM2.5). EPA approval depends on demonstration that the SIP contains adequate provisions to prevent significant contribution to nonattainment or interference with maintenance in other states.

rubrics_metrics.name: SIP revisions must not interfere with attainment/maintenance of NAAQS
rubrics_metrics.description: Revisions to state rules (e.g., construction permit requirements) 'do not interfere with the State's ability to attain or maintain the National Ambient Air Quality Standards (NAAQS), reasonable further progress (RFP) or other Clean Air Act (CAA) requirements.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA approves state regulatory updates only when they are shown not to impede attainment, maintenance, RFP, or other statutory obligations; administrative or fee updates are evaluated against this standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment of state definitions with EPA regulatory definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: State SIP revisions that amend regulatory definitions (example: Virginia's definition of volatile organic compound (VOC)) are evaluated for alignment with the EPA's regulatory definition of the term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approval is appropriate when the state definition is amended to align with EPA regulatory definition; ensures consistent application of federal standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Redesignation to attainment criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA will approve a state's request to redesignate an area to attainment for a NAAQS (example: 2012 annual PM2.5) when the state's submission satisfies applicable CAA requirements for redesignation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Though specific statutory criteria are not restated in every summary, EPA's approval implies the state must demonstrate attainment, maintenance plan, and other statutory elements required by the CAA for redesignation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval of delegation/partial program delegation
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA codifies approval of a state's or local agency's request for delegation of authority to implement and enforce a Federal plan or particular program elements (example: delegation for existing sewage sludge incineration units; partial delegation for CAA 112(r) RMP for agricultural anhydrous ammonia facilities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delegation approvals frequently specify the scope and limits of delegated authority (EPA may retain authority for aspects or for chemicals not meeting particular definitions). Approval is based on the adequacy of the requesting agency's ability to implement and enforce the delegated elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal plan implementation and enforcement standard
rubrics_metrics.description: The Federal plan addresses the implementation and enforcement of the emission guidelines applicable to existing affected units located in areas not covered by an approved and currently effective state plan; the Federal plan imposes emission limits and other control requirements for existing affected facilities which will reduce designated pollutants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a federal plan applies, EPA implements enforceable emission limits and controls; state/local delegations must be consistent with those federal plan requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pesticide tolerance and registration-review standard (FFDCA/FIFRA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FFDCA), and during FIFRA registration review, EPA reviews all aspects of a pesticide case, including existing tolerances, to ensure that the pesticide continues to meet the standard for registration under FIFRA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA action finalizing tolerances or tolerance changes follows its assessment during registration review that tolerances are necessary/appropriate and that the pesticide satisfies statutory safety/registration criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption from requirement of a tolerance (FFDCA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations may establish an exemption from the requirement of a tolerance for residues of specified substances when used as inert ingredients in pesticide formulations (examples include inert ingredient exemptions limited to no more than 10% by weight of the pesticide formulation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An exemption eliminates the need to establish a maximum permissible residue level when the substance is used in accordance with the terms of the exemption (e.g., usage limits, commodity restrictions). EPA approvals reference petition submissions and the terms under which exemptions apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: NSPS/EG technical amendment standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments to New Source Performance Standards (NSPS) and Emission Guidelines (EG) may finalize discrete technical changes (examples: temporary flaring provisions, vent gas net heating value continuous monitoring requirements, alternative performance test options) without altering other aspects of a prior final rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA may grant reconsideration on discrete aspects and finalize targeted technical corrections; such amendments should not change the substantive emission standards unless explicitly stated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory text correction and reinstatement standard
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA may issue corrections to inadvertent typographical errors or reinstatements of mistakenly deleted regulatory text (example: reinstating reporting requirements in 40 CFR 60.5420b(b)(1)–(15)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corrections are administrative in nature and 'do not affect the substantive requirements' of the original final rule; they ensure regulatory text accuracy and OFR formatting compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonably Available Control Technology (RACT) and contingency measures requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: States must meet applicable CAA requirements for Serious area contingency measures as well as RACT for certain stationary sources; SIP submissions addressing these elements are approved only when they meet statutory requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA reviews state-adopted regulatory revisions for specific source categories (e.g., landfill/biogas engines, refinery heaters) and may take partial approvals when specific submissions contain identified errors or when EPA is not taking action on certain sub-elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regional Haze program reasonable-progress and visibility protection standard
rubrics_metrics.description: State Implementation Plans for regional haze must satisfy applicable requirements under the Clean Air Act and EPA's Regional Haze Rule (RHR), including long-term strategies for making reasonable progress toward preventing and remedying anthropogenic impairment of visibility in Class I Federal areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA approval of regional haze SIP elements is contingent on demonstration of reasonable progress, long-term strategy, and other RHR elements for the implementation period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finding of failure to attain and reclassification authority
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA makes final findings that areas failed to attain the NAAQS by the attainment date and may reclassify areas (example: tribal portions of Greater Connecticut reclassified to Serious for the 2015 ozone NAAQS).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such findings fulfill EPA statutory obligations and may be accompanied by EPA actions on exceptional events requests and determinations of concurrence/nonconcurrence with state submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: State operating permit inclusion in SIP standard
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA may approve the inclusion of a revised state operating permit into a SIP when the permit limits specific emissions (example: visibility-impairing emissions from a pulp and paper mill) and the revision is consistent with the CAA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inclusion approval is taken under CAA provisions; EPA evaluates whether the permit revision adequately addresses applicable SIP requirements and source-specific controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative and minor rule revision approval standard
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA will take direct final action to approve administrative changes to state rules (examples: removal of references to revoked state regulations, updating fees, minor wording changes) when they are consistent with the Clean Air Act and applicable EPA regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative changes are approvable if they do not alter substantive obligations under the SIP or hinder attainment/maintenance of NAAQS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retention of EPA authority in partial delegations
rubrics_metrics.description: When EPA grants partial program delegation (example: partial delegation for agricultural anhydrous ammonia facilities), EPA retains authority for items outside the delegated scope (e.g., anhydrous ammonia not meeting the definition, RMP for other regulated chemicals, and RMP generally in the state for other facilities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delegation instruments should clearly define the boundaries of delegated vs. retained authority to avoid enforcement/implementation gaps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and administrative start-date rule for reporting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA can revise the start of a reporting period for a reporting and recordkeeping rule (example: PFAS Reporting Rule submission period start moved to January 31, 2027, or 60 days following the effective date of a forthcoming final rule, whichever is earlier).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such scheduling decisions set compliance timelines and are part of the administrative framework for information collection and reporting obligations.
